issues.title: Rename GroupMember resource to GroupMembership
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The resource type name `GroupMember` reads ambiguously against its own URI pattern: `GET /GroupMembers/{id}` looks like "get the members of group {id}" rather than "get a single membership record." It can also be misread as a subclass of User.

Change, to be made consistently across the draft:
- Resource type name: `GroupMember` → `GroupMembership`
- Endpoint: `/GroupMembers` → `/GroupMemberships`
- Schema URN: `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:GroupMember` → `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:GroupMembership`
- All prose references, JSON examples, and the IANA considerations entry

This is a mechanical, whole-document rename with no other content changes bundled in.

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body: Resolved via #13 (rename) and #14 (follow-on mechanical fixes, stacked on #13). Both merged.

issues.title: Add problem-evidence examples to the Introduction
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The Introduction currently argues the scalability problem in the abstract (payload size math) without grounding it in real deployment behavior. Add vendor-neutral example evidence:

- A documented case of a SCIM service provider limiting or refusing to support enumeration of group members at scale.
- A documented case of a SCIM client excluding the `members` attribute during sync because it cannot reliably deserialize very large membership payloads, and as a result has no way to reconcile membership drift against the service provider's actual state — it can only push add/remove operations, not verify state.

Goal: show the problem already causes client-side workarounds in production, without naming specific vendors or products.

issues.title: Add per-page limit and streaming-pagination guidance for unconstrained GET /GroupMemberships
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
`GET /GroupMemberships` without a filter returns all memberships across all groups, which a naive implementation could compute expensively. Keep unconstrained queries allowed (for consistency with SCIM's querying model and to leave room for future change-tracking extensions), but add guidance:

- Service providers SHOULD impose a reasonable per-page limit on `GroupMembership` listing (e.g., a maximum of 1000 results per page).
- Note that an implementation MAY sort results internally by `group.id` to stream pagination across group boundaries without materializing the entire membership dataset.

issues.title: Add explicit normative language on display optionality
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Returning `display` for both `group` and `member` sub-attributes may be unnecessary payload weight for large result sets. The schema already permits omitting it (`required: false`, `mutability: readOnly`), but the draft doesn't say so explicitly. Add normative language along these lines:

"Service providers MAY optimize payload size by omitting display names entirely, or by configuring them as `returned: \"request\"` (available only when explicitly requested via the `attributes` query parameter). Because `display` is optional and read-only, a service provider that never implements it is fully conformant."

issues.title: Replace membersMetadata's policy/ref/memberCount with a single externally-managed boolean; remove allowedMemberTypes
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Restructure the `membersMetadata` Group schema extension:

- Drop `ref`: redundant, since any client can construct the filter URI from the pattern the draft already defines.
- Drop `memberCount`: expensive to compute for exactly the large groups this draft targets.
- Replace the `policy` enum (`inline`/`external`/`hybrid`) with a single boolean attribute named `externallyManaged`, signaling "this group's membership is managed externally via `/GroupMemberships` and not shown here." A group can carry the flag regardless of whether `members` happens to be populated, removing the need for a distinct "hybrid" value.
- Drop `allowedMemberTypes` entirely: it's a general-purpose Group-resource improvement unrelated to this draft's pagination problem, not a `GroupMembership`-specific concern. The right home for it is a future, separate Group schema extension, not yet written.
- Update the extension's schema URN segment from `groupMembers` to `groupMemberships`, to stay consistent with the resource rename in #3: `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:groupMemberships:2.0:Group`.

Resulting extension: a single top-level boolean attribute (`externallyManaged`), a direct attribute of the extension namespace — no wrapper attribute, no enum, no `ref`, no `memberCount`, no `allowedMemberTypes`.

issues.title: Fix incorrect per-instance returned:"never" guidance in Service Provider Considerations
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft's Service Provider Considerations section implies a service provider can set `returned: "never"` on the `Group.members` attribute on a per-Group-resource-instance basis. This is incorrect: `returned` is a schema-level property applied uniformly to a resource type via the `/Schemas` definition, not something that varies per resource instance.

Action: locate this language, confirm it's still present, and remove or rewrite it to correctly describe schema-level (not instance-level) declarations. Final wording may depend on the outcome of the membersMetadata restructuring issue, since that also touches how service providers declare per-group membership-management behavior.

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body: Closing as superseded: the `external`/`hybrid` policy language this issue refers to was removed by the membersMetadata restructuring in #15, commit https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/commit/cbdeebe (#7).

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body: Superseded by #7's removal of the external/hybrid policy language; see prior comment.

issues.title: Require member.type filtering when a service provider supports more than one member resource type
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft currently gives a SHOULD for service providers to support filtering on `member.type`. A SHOULD leaves clients unable to distinguish "filtering isn't supported at all" from "filtering is supported, but `member.type` specifically isn't a valid filter attribute here" — both surface identically (e.g. a `400 invalidFilter`), which is especially costly for large, heterogeneous groups where the client's only fallback is enumerating and filtering client-side.

Change: if a service provider supports more than one resource type as a group member, it MUST support filtering on `member.type`. A service provider with only one possible member type is unaffected, since the condition doesn't apply.

issues.title: Clarify core-schema immutability rationale and scope the membership availability requirement to authorization
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Two related clarifications to the resource's mutability model:

**1. Core schema immutability, explained rather than method-banned.** The core `group` and `member` attributes are already declared immutable in the schema. Add prose explaining why, rather than separately stating the resource "MUST only support POST, GET, and DELETE": a `GroupMembership` is fundamentally a link between two resources, so the link itself isn't meant to change — a different group or member value represents a different membership, not an edit to this one. This does not ban PATCH/PUT as methods; it simply means the core schema gives them nothing to act on. A service provider that adds its own mutable extension attributes may support PATCH for those without contradicting this document.

**2. Availability requirement, scoped to authorization.** If a service provider supports the `GroupMembership` resource, it MUST make available via `/GroupMemberships` every membership that the authenticated and authorized SCIM client is authorized to view. This is independent of whether `Group.members` is also supported or returned — a service provider MAY choose not to return `Group.members` for groups whose membership is exposed via `GroupMembership`, and this requirement does not mandate supporting `Group.members` at all.

issues.title: Add display-consistency rule for group and member sub-attributes
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body: When populated, the `display` sub-attribute on `group` or `member` MUST match the current `displayName` of the referenced `Group` or `User` resource. This closes an existing ambiguity: today nothing prevents a service provider from returning a stale or divergent label from the referenced resource's own canonical `displayName`.

issues.title: Remove "Discovering Support" / "Service Provider Considerations" headers; relocate consistency content and drop non-normative discovery MUSTs
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Remove the "Discovering Support for the GroupMembership Resource" section and its parent "Service Provider Considerations" section entirely. Specifically:

- Drop "service providers that support the `GroupMembership` resource MUST declare this support in their `ResourceType` and `Schema` metadata" — a generic protocol-level discovery statement with no corresponding normative basis in RFC7644 (which only describes, rather than mandates, that service providers extending resource types publish them in `/ResourceTypes` and their schemas in `/Schemas`). Patching that gap belongs at the protocol level, not in this draft.
- Drop the `Schema Endpoint` subsection's "the `/Schemas` response MUST include the full schema definitions" sentence, for the same reason.
- Relocate the `Group.members`/`GroupMembership` consistency requirement and example (currently under "Impact on the Group Resource") into the "Managing GroupMembership Resources" section — it's about runtime behavioral consistency, not discovery, and doesn't belong under either removed header.
- Add a short, non-normative pointer sentence near the top of Section 2 ("The GroupMembership Resource"), before the JSON Representation and Resource Type Representation examples: "This resource's `ResourceType` and `Schema` definitions are discoverable via the `/ResourceTypes` and `/Schemas` endpoints, respectively, per [RFC7644]. The definitions for both are provided below."

issues.title: Fix missing opening quote in the group.value filter example
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Reported by Paul Lanzi in his review of draft-zollner-scim-group-members-01 on the SCIM list (item 8), and acknowledged in the 2026-07-14 reply.

The "find all members of a group" example in the Filtering section is missing the opening quote before the filter value, so the example is not a valid SCIM filter. It should match the quoting used in the `member.type` example below it.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L297

issues.title: Remove performance-only framing from cursor pagination description
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Reported by Paul Lanzi (item 7), agreed in the 2026-07-14 reply.

The cursor pagination bullet says cursors are for "improved performance with very large data sets." That implies cursors are only useful at scale. Cursor pagination also provides a stable result set while a client pages slowly through the data, which is relevant for any membership listing. The line is also a sentence fragment, unlike the index-based bullet above it.

Change: state that cursor pagination per RFC9865 is available as an alternative to index-based pagination, without the performance qualifier.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L284

issues.title: Clarify how clients retrieve collections of GroupMembership resources
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Reported by Paul Lanzi (item 6), agreed in the 2026-07-14 reply.

The Retrieving section says clients can retrieve "a list of resources," which implies a way to submit a list of memberships to fetch. No such mechanism exists. In practice a collection is retrieved by listing, typically narrowed with a filter on `group.value`, `member.value`, or other attributes. SCIM can OR multiple ids in a filter, but that is awkward at scale and not the primary use case.

Change: say that clients retrieve a membership by `id`, or retrieve a collection that can be narrowed with a filter.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L271

issues.title: Add member-side access guidance to Security Considerations
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Reported by Paul Lanzi (item 9), agreed in the 2026-07-14 reply.

Security Considerations covers one direction: access to a `Group` alone does not imply access to its member list. It does not cover the reverse. A client that can read a `User` (or any other member resource) but is not authorized to see that resource's group memberships could learn them by querying `/GroupMemberships?filter=member.value eq "X"`, including whether the member belongs to any group at all (`totalResults > 0`). The membership edge can be more sensitive than either the member or the group individually (for example, membership in a restricted investigation or privileged-admin group).

Change: add a symmetric bullet stating that access to a member resource does not imply access to its memberships, and that `member.value` filtering is subject to the same authorization as reading `Group.members`. This applies to any member resource type, not only `User`.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L541

issues.title: Show the request that produces each Group example response
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Reported by Paul Lanzi (item 2), agreed in the 2026-07-14 reply.

The two Group examples in "Example Group Resources" show a response with no indication of the request that returned it. Paul's point was that readers benefit from seeing the URI that produced the output. His review predates the removal of the `policy` and `ref` attributes, so the original external and hybrid example references are gone, but the same point applies to the current two examples.

Change: add the `GET /scim/v2/Groups/{id}` request above each example response.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L180-L232

issues.title: Correct "ResourceType schema" wording in Resource Type Representation
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Raised by Matthias Winter in his first review (item 13f), accepted as a prose consistency pass and deferred until the Service Provider Considerations restructuring landed.

The sentence conflates the `ResourceType` resource type with its own schema. The `/ResourceTypes` endpoint returns `ResourceType` resources; it does not return a "schema." Fixing it here sets the precedent for the wider schema-versus-resource terminology check.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L145

issues.title: Replace `externallyManaged` with a `membersEmbedded` delivery guarantee
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Raised by Matthias Winter in the thread on draft-zollner-scim-group-members-01 (2026-09-04 and 2026-09-07).

Matthias asked which of two goals `externallyManaged` serves: per-group authority over where memberships are managed, or a signal that helps clients that don't support `GroupMembership`. The draft's text mixes the two. The attribute name and the "canonical and preferred source" wording read as per-group management authority. The completeness requirement for `/GroupMemberships` reads as the compatibility goal. A per-group authority split also conflicts with that requirement.

The intent is the compatibility goal. The attribute is replaced by `membersEmbedded`, a statement of what the service provider guarantees about `members` for each group:
- `true`: the full current membership is in `members`, so an omitted or empty `members` means no members.
- `false`: `members` is not guaranteed to hold the full membership; use `/GroupMemberships`.
- absent: no statement (plain RFC7643 behavior).

The draft currently says absence means `members` is canonical, which is wrong for legacy service providers that return partial lists. The change also states that the attribute says nothing about mutability or authority, that a service provider returning the extension MUST support `GroupMembership`, that service providers using only `GroupMembership` may omit both `Group.members` and the extension, and that a service provider supporting the extension SHOULD list it in its Group resource type's `schemaExtensions`.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/8bfdd9e4cea8b17727cb6343ec854c967bf66679/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L166-L178

issues.title: Align IANA Considerations with the RFC7643 registry and registration template
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The IANA Considerations section names the wrong registry and does not use the RFC7643 schema registration template, which an RFC registering schema URIs must include in the document body. The extension description also predates the `membersEmbedded` change. Security Considerations and IANA Considerations are also nested one level too deep, under Schema Representation.

Needed:
- Add a Schema Registration Templates section to the body for both URNs.
- Reduce IANA Considerations to a request that references those templates, using the correct registry name.
- Update the extension description to say it indicates whether all of a group's memberships are embedded in `members`.
- Promote Security Considerations and IANA Considerations to top-level sections.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7328c08ca78bc26f514466d6f24cdb7e524ab3d6/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L536-L556

issues.title: Fix inconsistencies found in a full-document review
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
A read-through of the current draft found a few inconsistencies.

- One RFC7644 citation points to the wrong section: Security Considerations is Section 7, not Section 8.
- The unconstrained-listing paragraph refers to `group.id`, but the attribute is `group.value`.
- The extension schema `name` has no spaces, unlike the core schema `name` and the registration template.
- "Extension schema" and "schema extension" are both used; RFC7643 uses "schema extension".
- The pointer to the `ResourceType` and `Schema` definitions says "below" without saying where.
- `member.$ref` restricts `referenceTypes` to `User` and `Group`, but the draft says a member can be any resource type. The schema should be marked as illustrative.
- Typo: "scaleable".

Needed: correct each of the above.

issues.title: Define what happens to memberships when a group or member is deleted
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft doesn't say what happens to `GroupMembership` resources when the Group or member they reference is deleted. RFC7644 Section 3.6 requires a deleted resource to return 404 and be omitted from query results. Without a rule here, one service provider may keep dangling memberships pointing at deleted resources while another removes them, so clients reconciling membership state will see different results.

Change: when a Group or a member resource is deleted, the service provider MUST delete every `GroupMembership` that references it, and those deletions follow RFC7644 Section 3.6.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L240-L244

issues.title: State that a group and member pair has at most one GroupMembership
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft implies that a group and member pair maps to a single membership, through the 409 rule on duplicate creates, but never says so. SCIM schemas can't declare uniqueness across two attributes, so the rule has to be in the prose. Because `GroupMembership` represents only direct memberships, a second resource for the same pair is always an error, never a separate path.

Change: a service provider MUST NOT maintain more than one `GroupMembership` with the same `group.value` and `member.value`.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L60
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L255

issues.title: Explain how to remove a membership without knowing its id
issues.author: Zollnerd

issues.title: Specify `scimType` `uniqueness` for duplicate membership creates
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
A duplicate POST must return 409, but the draft doesn't name a `scimType`. RFC7644 Section 3.3 says a create that conflicts with an existing resource MUST return 409 with a `scimType` of `uniqueness`. The draft also doesn't rule out treating a duplicate POST as a success. Some service providers will be tempted to make it idempotent, which breaks clients that decide what to do next based on the status code.

Change: require 409 with `scimType` `uniqueness`, per RFC7644 Section 3.3, and state that the service provider MUST NOT create a second resource or return a success response.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L255

issues.title: Make invalid-reference errors a MUST and cover disallowed member types and nesting cycles
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
When the referenced group or member doesn't exist, the draft says the service provider SHOULD return 400 `invalidValue`. Because it's a SHOULD, service providers can return 404, 409, or 500 instead, and clients can't reliably tell a bad reference apart from other failures. The draft also says nothing about two related failures:
- a member whose resource type the group doesn't accept, for example a Group member when nested groups aren't supported;
- a membership that would create a nesting cycle when the service provider forbids cycles.

Change: make the 400 `invalidValue` response a MUST, and apply it to all three cases.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L253

issues.title: Discuss relaxing the `display` consistency requirement from MUST to SHOULD
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Issue #11 added a rule that, when populated, `group.display` and `member.display` MUST match the current `displayName` of the referenced resource. I'm in favor of relaxing this to a SHOULD and opening it for WG discussion before changing the text.

The MUST is costly at the scale this draft targets. Renaming a group with a million members would require the service provider to update, or join at read time, a million `GroupMembership` representations to stay conformant. That's the kind of fan-out the resource is meant to avoid. The same section also says the value "generally" corresponds to `displayName`, which already reads like a SHOULD. And `displayName` is optional on User, so it's unclear what a conformant `member.display` holds when the User has no `displayName`.

Proposed direction: `display` SHOULD reflect the referenced resource's current `displayName`, and clients MUST NOT rely on `display` to identify or match resources. Views from implementers who maintain denormalized display values would be especially useful.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L84
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L101

issues.title: Update the parent Group's `meta` when a membership is created or deleted
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
When a service provider exposes `Group.members`, creating or deleting a `GroupMembership` changes how the Group is represented. Clients that use `If-Match` or compare `meta.version` and `meta.lastModified` on Groups need those values to change too, otherwise they will treat a stale cached Group as current.

The reverse should be stated as well. A change to a Group that doesn't change a given membership doesn't modify that `GroupMembership`. Examples are a `displayName` change, which affects only the derived `group.display`, or adding or removing other members. Such a change MUST NOT alter the membership's `meta.lastModified` or `meta.version`.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L244

issues.title: Clarify read-only signaling and errors when POST or DELETE is unsupported
issues.author: Zollnerd

issues.title: Clarify the `membersEmbedded` definition and how it applies to `attributes` and `excludedAttributes`
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The definition has two problems.

First, a client that excludes `members` (`excludedAttributes=members`), or requests `attributes` without `members`, gets a Group with no `members` alongside `membersEmbedded: true`. Read literally, the definition of `true` means that group has no members.

Second, the definition is a single paragraph covering `true`, `false`, and absent. The sentence telling clients to use `/GroupMemberships` sits inside the `false` description but reads as if it always applies.

Change:
- limit the `true` guarantee to responses where `members` would be returned given the request's `attributes` and `excludedAttributes` (RFC7644 Section 3.4.2.5);
- split the definition into one paragraph per value;
- make the SHOULD explicitly conditional on `false` and on the client needing the complete membership.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L174-L176

issues.title: Note why `group.value` and `member.value` are case-exact
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
In the `GroupMembership` schema, `group.value` and `member.value` are `caseExact: true`, while `members.value` in the RFC7643 Group schema is `caseExact: false`. `true` is the correct choice. These values hold resource ids, and RFC7643 Section 3.1 defines `id` as case-exact. A short note keeps readers from reading the difference as a mistake or "fixing" it to match RFC7643.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L386-L396
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L430-L440
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L488

issues.title: State that both `GroupMembership` and `Group.members` hold only direct memberships
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft says `GroupMembership` represents direct memberships only, but says nothing about `Group.members`. The draft requires the two to stay consistent, so `Group.members` is limited to direct members by implication. It should say so explicitly, so a service provider doesn't flatten nested groups into `members`. The draft should also state that transitive membership is out of scope. In RFC7643 it is exposed through `User.groups`, which Section 4.1.2 allows to hold both direct and indirect memberships.

Open question: should a service provider that supports `GroupMembership` be required (MUST) to include only direct members in `Group.members`, or only recommended to (SHOULD)? A MUST is a new constraint for service providers that currently flatten nested groups into `members`. A SHOULD leaves open a mismatch with the consistency requirement between `Group.members` and `GroupMembership`. Decision deferred.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L60
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L244

issues.title: Make pagination support discoverable, recommend cursors, and show a complete cursor request
issues.author: Zollnerd

issues.title: Allow `tooMany` for unfiltered listings, require stable ordering, and make the sorting note non-normative
issues.author: Zollnerd

issues.title: Require `eq` filtering and the combined group-and-member filter
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft requires filtering on `group.value` and `member.value` but doesn't name an operator. It also doesn't require the two to be combined. The combined filter is the basic reconciliation query (does this specific membership exist, and what is its id?), and the guidance on removing a membership without its id (#32) depends on it.

Change:
- require the `eq` operator for `group.value`, `member.value`, and `member.type` filtering;
- require `group.value` and `member.value` filters combined with `and`, and add an example.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L296-L312

issues.title: Define `member.type` values as ResourceType names
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The draft requires `member.type` filtering when a service provider supports more than one member resource type, but never says what strings `member.type` holds. A client can't build `member.type eq "User"` reliably if one service provider returns `"User"`, another `"user"`, and a third a URN.

The natural anchor is the `ResourceType` `name` (RFC7643 Section 6), which is also what `meta.resourceType` contains. RFC7643 erratum 8475 (Verified) makes ResourceType `name` case-exact, so `member.type` should be `caseExact: true` as well. `member.type` stays readOnly; this only defines the value the service provider puts there.

Change: `member.type` MUST be the `name` of the member's `ResourceType`, and the schema sets `caseExact` to `true`.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L97-L98
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L454-L463

issues.title: Remove `bulkId` from the DELETE operation in the Bulk example
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The Bulk example puts a `bulkId` on its DELETE operation. RFC7644 Section 3.7 defines `bulkId` as a transient identifier for a newly created resource, so that later operations in the same request can refer to it. On a DELETE it has no effect and suggests a use that doesn't exist.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L354-L358

issues.title: Don't reveal unauthorized groups, members, or memberships through errors or `totalResults`
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The create rules let a client learn which resources exist. A POST with arbitrary ids returns 400 `invalidValue` if a referenced resource doesn't exist and 409 if the membership does, so the caller learns whether groups, users, and memberships exist even without read access. `totalResults` on filtered queries can leak the same information, for example a member count for a group the client can't read.

Change: add a Security Considerations requirement that service providers MUST NOT reveal through errors or `totalResults` the existence of resources the client isn't authorized to read, and SHOULD return the same response for an unreadable reference as for a nonexistent one.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L253-L255
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L546-L552

issues.title: Reword membership authorization rules as equivalent authorization rather than required grants
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
The Security Considerations say a client that can read `Group.members` MUST be granted permission to GET the matching `GroupMembership` resources. The aim is that the two paths get the same authorization, but as written it requires a grant. That stops a service provider from applying a stricter policy to the new endpoint, and the requirement belongs to the authorization model, which this draft leaves to service providers. The write-side bullet has the same shape: a client authorized to PATCH `Group.members` MUST have equivalent POST and DELETE permissions.

Change: for both bullets, require the service provider to apply equivalent authorization to the `GroupMembership` operations as to the corresponding `Group.members` read or write, rather than requiring a grant.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L548
https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L552

issues.title: Note the availability risk of large membership queries
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Unfiltered or broadly filtered queries on `/GroupMemberships`, and the joins needed to fill `display` sub-attributes, can be expensive at the scale this draft targets, and can be abused to degrade availability. Add a non-normative Security Considerations bullet pointing to the per-page limits and the `tooMany` error.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/7d2bee0bd3d443a629d6564b8c8ed23f94fb3907/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L294

issues.title: Editorial fixes from a full-document review
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
- The paragraph on omitting `display` sits inside the attribute definition list, between `member` and `meta`. Move it after `meta`.
- The sentence on building the membership query URI still refers to a "service-provider-supplied value", which was the removed `ref` attribute. Reword it as a plain description of the query.
- The `groupMemberships` extension is described in Section 5 and again in the "Usage" subsection of Schema Representation. Remove the duplicated Usage subsection and the repeated intro sentence, keeping only the schema definition. The requirement to list the extension URN in `schemas` already comes from RFC7643 Section 3; add a pointer to it in Section 5.
- The POST example request line is outside a code span and has no `/scim/v2` prefix, unlike every other example. Format it the same way as the other examples.
- The `members` value in the "`membersEmbedded` set to `true`" Group example has only `value` and `display`. Add `$ref` and `type` so it shows the full shape.

issues.title: Reconcile the duplicate-create 409 with the rule against revealing unauthorized memberships
issues.author: Zollnerd
issues.body:
Two MUSTs added in the full-document review conflict for some clients.

The Creating section requires a `409 Conflict` with `uniqueness` when a POST duplicates an existing membership (#33). The Security Considerations require that error responses not reveal the existence of a `GroupMembership` the client isn't authorized to read (#50). Read and write authorization are separate checks (#51), so a client can be allowed to add members to a group without being allowed to read its memberships. For that client, the 409 reveals that the membership exists, which the security requirement forbids.

Learning whether a member is already in a group is inherent in being allowed to add members to it, so the 409 is not a leak worth preventing. Change: state that a client authorized to add members to a group can learn from the 409 whether a member already belongs to it, and that this does not violate the requirement. The non-disclosure requirement then applies to clients with neither read nor write access to the group.

https://github.com/Zollnerd/scim-group-membership/blob/419a4cbe31426d2cbe63b70fcc1d15c840b88784/draft-zollner-scim-group-membership.md?plain=1#L274

pulls.author: drmawi
pulls.body:
Substantial changes:

- Removed the extension schema (see my last e-mail)
- Renamed the resource to GroupMembership, as suggested by Hans-Joerg
- One paragraph disallowed any changes of GroupMembership resources. This is correct for the core resource as defined in the draft, which can only be created or deleted, but SCIM 2.0 allows service providers to add more attributes (e.g. through schema extensions), and those attributes may be changable. Potential use-cases are, for example, an expiration date for a membership, comments, or attributes that flag the membership as protected or primary.

Clarifications:

- Remarks on the relation to the User.groups attribute
- Improved definition of the GroupMembership attributes
- Some more minor issues, see commit messages

comments.author: Zollnerd
comments.body:
Hi Matthias,

Thanks for putting this together, and thank you for the thorough pass on the draft’s wording and structure. 

I’ve reviewed this commit by commit. While several of the individual improvements are solid, I won’t be merging this PR as a whole. A couple of overarching reasons:

* **Scope & Granularity:** This bundles a wide variety of independent changes into a single PR (a resource rename, schema extension removal, new normative requirements, textual fixes, and structural overhaul). Reviewing and merging these together makes it difficult to evaluate each on its own merits. In standards work, these need to stand or fall independently.
* **Authorship:** One commit adds you as a co-author of the draft. In IETF/standards processes, adding an author or editor is a significant decision that is made based on a long-term co-editing commitment, rather than something introduced via an unsolicited PR. That said, given the multiple rounds of feedback and valuable discussions we’ve already had on the draft, I’d be very happy to include you in the **Acknowledgements** or **Contributors** section to recognize your input.

That said, many of your ideas are valuable. To handle this cleanly while preserving commit history where appropriate, I’ll be cherry-picking clean commits directly and manually implementing reworked versions of the others. 

Here is how each point is being handled:

### 1. Accepted as Written (Cherry-picking directly)
* **Rename `GroupMember` to `GroupMembership`** (`0bbd1fd`): Agreed. Tracked in #3.
* **Capitalization, `$ref` JSON completeness, and meta sub-attributes fixes** (`653fefb`, `5048090`, `6a29ef8`): Clean fixes, cherry-picking directly.

These have been merged in to main via PRs #13 and #14.

### 2. Partially Accepted / Reworked (Implementing separately)
* **`membersMetadata` Extension** (`963e15d`): Rather than removing it outright, I'm simplifying it to a single boolean attribute and dropping `ref`, `memberCount`, `policy`, and `allowedMemberTypes`. Tracked in #7.
* **PATCH/PUT restrictions & membership availability** (`579483`): Reworked rather than adopted as written. Tracked in #10.
* **Expanded Attribute Descriptions** (`4e2f786`): The display-consistency point is good and will be incorporated. However, I’m not adopting the `User.groups` consistency requirement: `User.groups` can include indirect/transitive memberships, whereas `Group.members` and `GroupMembership` are strictly direct-only, so a blanket consistency requirement does not hold. The restated mutability/required constraints are also already covered by the schema definitions. Tracked in #11.
* **Service Provider Considerations / Discovering Support** (`49ef366`, `885636d`, `fe030b0`): Removing these headers and the two "MUST declare support" statements entirely, as neither has a normative basis in RFC 7644 and this draft is not the right vehicle to patch that gap. Tracked in #12.
* **"Attributes vs. Properties" Precision** (`ea51f2e`): Will be folded into a dedicated terminology pass once the structural changes land.

### 3. Not Adopted
* **Deleting "Impact on the Group Resource"** (`5ae36c4`): Not adopting; this content is not duplicated elsewhere. It will be relocated rather than deleted as part of #12.

---

I appreciate the time and effort you put into this review. Moving forward, please submit contributions like these as smaller, focused PRs or GitHub issues so each topic can be discussed and evaluated separately. 

Thank you,

Danny

pulls.title: Replace externallyManaged with membersEmbedded delivery guarantee
pulls.author: Zollnerd
pulls.body:
Fixes #22.

Responds to Matthias Winter's 2026-09-07 question on the list about what externallyManaged is for. The old name and text read as per-group management authority, which conflicts with the requirement that /GroupMemberships expose every membership. The attribute is now `membersEmbedded`, a statement of what the service provider guarantees about `members` for each group:

- `true`: the full current membership is in `members`; omitted or empty means no members
- `false`: `members` is not guaranteed to hold the full membership; use /GroupMemberships
- absent: no statement (plain RFC7643 behavior)

Also: a service provider including the extension MUST support GroupMembership, SHOULD list the extension in its Group ResourceType's schemaExtensions, and the text no longer treats absence as "canonical". The attribute does not affect mutability or indicate a preferred management method.

This branch and paul-lanzi-review-feedback both edit the Group example section; whichever merges second will need a small conflict resolution.
